rfm_tuples.R: Going-concern / audit-quality integrity — clean KPMG audit opinion, no substantial-doubt language, internal controls effective.
rfm_tuples.f: If true: no ASC 205-40 'substantial doubt' phrasing in 10-K; no Item 4.01 auditor-change 8-Ks; no Big 4 resignation; no disagreements.
rfm_tuples.M_value: going_concern: NO_GOING_CONCERN (0 matches in latest 10-K filed 2026-03-19). auditor_change_tracker: CLEAN_AUDITOR_TENURE (0 Item 4.01 filings in 5y, 0 Big4 resignations, 0 disagreements). KPMG continues as registered public accounting firm (PCAOB ID 185).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Universal audit-quality screen clean; KPMG tenure undisturbed; no going-concern signal at the audit layer.

rfm_tuples.R: Liquidity claim — $502.5M total liquid resources ($163M cash + $339.5M marketable securities) management states is 'sufficient to meet working capital needs, capital expenditures and financing obligations for at least the next 12 months and over the long-term.'
rfm_tuples.f: If true, post-cutoff capital actions (notably the $125M ASR announced March 13, 2026) should not materially impair liquidity, and there should be no debt-maturity wall or contingent claim that consumes the cushion. No long-term debt should be disclosed.
rfm_tuples.M_source: Filing-internal balance sheet + Liquidity section + Subsequent Events.
rfm_tuples.M_value: $502.5M liquid resources at 1/31/26. NO long-term debt disclosed. Contractual purchase commitments only $117.2M ($70.9M within 12 mo). HOWEVER: $125M ASR consummated March 13, 2026 (post-balance-sheet, pre-cutoff) drains ~25% of liquidity in a single transaction; remaining $75M of 2026 authorization still available at company discretion. Pro-forma liquid resources fall to ~$377.5M before considering Q1 FY27 OCF. OCF FY26 $159.2M (2.1x FY25 $77.6M) so internal generation is real.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Liquidity comfortable; no debt wall; ASR is meaningful drawdown but management retained ~$378M cushion + $159M annual OCF generation. Sufficiency-of-funds claim survives quantitative test.

rfm_tuples.R: Customer base claim — '1,677 customers' and '59% of the Fortune 100 companies' as customers; positioned as proof of enterprise traction.
rfm_tuples.f: If Fortune-100 customer relationships are material, they should leave evidence in counterparty filings (megacap 10-Ks/10-Qs/8-Ks should reference Sprinklr at least occasionally as a vendor/technology partner). Customer count itself should not be eroding.
rfm_tuples.M_value: megacap_namecheck: signal=INFLATION_SUSPECT. ZERO Sprinklr mentions across 17 megacap CIKs (Apple, Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta, Nvidia, Tesla, Walmart, Berkshire, JPMorgan, ExxonMobil, GM, Ford, Boeing, Lockheed, Honeywell, Caterpillar, Pfizer, JNJ) in 10y of 10-K/10-Q/8-K. ALSO: total customers DROPPED from 1,930 (1/31/25) to 1,677 (1/31/26) = -13.1% YoY net loss. Large customers (>=$1M ARR) DROPPED from 149 to 141 = -5.4%. Filing self-discloses 'strategic refinement of our customer profile' as the reason but does not break out gross-churn vs deliberate-exit.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Two independent obscuring signals: (1) Fortune-100 logos are real but no megacap discloses Sprinklr as a material vendor in SEC filings (consistent with small-line-item subscription buys, but undermines 'enterprise-grade-platform-of-choice' narrative weight); (2) absolute customer count down 253 net YoY is repackaged as a strategy choice. Neither is fatal; combined they point to a maturing/contracting commercial footprint.

rfm_tuples.R: Net income $22.9M FY26 — sustained GAAP profitability framed as core thesis underpinning $200M new buyback authorization.
rfm_tuples.f: If profitability is structurally improving, GAAP NI should be flat-to-growing YoY and operating cash flow should corroborate.
rfm_tuples.M_source: Filing-internal income statement (FY26 vs FY25 vs FY24) + cash-flow statement.
rfm_tuples.M_value: GAAP NI: FY26 $22.9M vs FY25 $121.6M vs FY24 $51.4M = -81% YoY and -55% vs FY24. PRIMARY driver: FY25 included a $73.3M income-tax BENEFIT (valuation-allowance release) that flipped to a $43.9M PROVISION in FY26 — a $117M swing entirely in the tax line. Pre-tax income actually GREW: $66.8M FY26 vs $48.3M FY25 = +38%. Operating income $40.2M vs $24.0M = +68%. Operating cash flow $159.2M vs $77.6M = +105%.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: GAAP NI collapse is mostly a tax-line normalization (FY25 was inflated by one-time VA release); operating metrics genuinely improved. BUT the filing presents the $22.9M NI without leading with the tax-normalization context in summary, which is technically truthful but obscurative. Quality of disclosure is mixed — not a fraud signal, but the headline number is much weaker than the underlying business.

rfm_tuples.R: Capital-return discipline — $150M of 2025 Share Repurchase Program FULLY COMPLETED in Q3 FY26; new $200M 2026 Program authorized March 11, 2026; $125M ASR executed March 13, 2026 — framed as confident counter-cyclical deployment at depressed prices.
rfm_tuples.f: If true, share repurchases should be executed at consistently low prices and reflect a coherent capital-allocation framework, not panic-buying after stock collapse.
rfm_tuples.M_source: Filing-internal Item 5 + Note 10 + Subsequent Events. Cross-checked against insider-sales price data from insider_vs_calendar.
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY26 actual: 17,616,548 shares retired at $8.54 avg for $150.4M (fully consumed 2025 auth). Insider sales (per insider_vs_calendar) executed at $7.12-$7.78 in Sep'25-Jan'26 — meaning company was buying at ~$8.54 avg while insiders were selling at $7.12-$7.78 (BELOW the company's buyback price). 2026 program $200M authorized 3/11/26; $125M ASR same week (3/13/26) = 62.5% of 2026 authorization burned in a single trade just 2 days post-announcement. Aggressive front-loading at trough, but reduces optionality.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Buyback execution is real and counter-cyclical at the corporate level, BUT insiders sold at LOWER prices than the company paid (negative price information asymmetry against shareholders). The 62%-in-2-days 2026 ASR exhausts most of the new authorization immediately, leaving little dry powder if stock falls further. Capital-return claim is procedurally honored but economically suboptimal vs insider behavior.

rfm_tuples.R: Insider trading discipline — Insider Trading Policy disclosed, sales described as ordinary-course; Founder/Chairman Ragy Thomas + executive team align with shareholders.
rfm_tuples.f: If true, insider sales should be 10b5-1-governed, modest in scale, and not abnormally clustered around adverse events or at trough prices.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Last 365d (5/20/25-5/20/26): 61 Form 4 filings, 56 sales totaling $97.4M. 14 proximate to events, $4.76M. CRITICAL DETAIL: Director Neeraj Agrawal sold 370,734 shares for ~$2.8M on Oct 6-8, 2025 (3 transactions at $7.51-$7.78) — NOT 10b5-1 (discretionary). Founder/Chairman Ragy Thomas sold 28,916 shares for $224K on Sep 16, 2025 at $7.75 — also NOT 10b5-1. CEO Rory Read sold 138,505 shares for $988K on Jan 14, 2026 at $7.13 — IS 10b5-1. Of 14 proximate sales, only 2 (14%) were 10b5-1; 12 (86%) were discretionary. Signal: CLUSTERED_DISCRETIONARY (downgraded to UNCONFIRMED only because validators require contractor-program-exposure linkage which doesn't apply to a pure-SaaS issuer).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Founder, a director, and multiple senior executives executed DISCRETIONARY (non-10b5-1) open-market sales at $7.13-$7.78 — i.e., at or below the company's own ~$8.54 buyback average. Discretionary sales by a founder/chairman near trough prices, while the company is simultaneously deploying $150M+ of corporate cash on buybacks at HIGHER prices, is a material misalignment signal. Total $97.4M of insider distribution over 12 months is large relative to a ~$1.5B market cap. This is the strongest mode-B finding.

rfm_tuples.R: Sprinklr Service product suite is positioned as a strategic growth pillar (one of four product suites: Social, Insights, Marketing, Service) — heavily invested R&D and sales effort.
rfm_tuples.f: If genuinely strategic and well-disclosed, Sprinklr Service should not be the subject of an active securities-fraud class action alleging the Company FAILED TO DISCLOSE material risks associated with it.

Moderate (not severe) because (a) provision is $0 and management has 'no opinion on outcome', (b) class period closed 6/5/24 well before cutoff, (c) the company has continued to publicly emphasize Sprinklr Service — either confident or doubling-down.

rfm_tuples.R: Operational restructuring — 12% workforce reduction implemented Feb 2025 (third reduction in three years: 4% Feb 2023, 3% May 2024, 12% Feb 2025) framed as cost-discipline to 'position the Company for long-term success.'
rfm_tuples.f: If genuinely a one-time realignment, restructuring should be complete with no further reductions announced; sales productivity should rebound; subscription gross margin should hold.
rfm_tuples.M_source: claim_evolution.query_claim_evolution(cik='0001569345', search_term='workforce reduction', base_filing_date='2025-03-21', cutoff_date='2026-05-20') + filing-internal Note 14 + MD&A gross-margin disclosure.
rfm_tuples.M_value: claim_evolution: 2 subsequent mentions, REAFFIRMED. Filing states 'we do not expect to incur any further restructuring expense' for the 2026/2025 plans. BUT: (a) THIRD consecutive annual restructuring (4% -> 3% -> 12% — accelerating, not declining), (b) Subscription gross margin DECLINED from 80% to 76% in FY26 — wrong direction for a 'realignment for long-term success', (c) Sales & marketing -10% YoY ($319.6M -> $287.6M) is consistent with the 12% RIF but management also notes 'we paused certain' sales/onboarding activities — same admission pattern as UPWK's Lifted disclosure, (d) Customer count -13% YoY tracks the sales-headcount cut.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Restructuring is real and disclosed but the three-year cadence (accelerating from 4% to 12%) and the simultaneous gross-margin compression + customer-count loss suggest the cuts are reactive to demand weakness rather than proactive realignment. Management's 'no further restructuring expected' is the same language used before each prior round.

summary: Sprinklr is structurally solvent (KPMG-clean audit, no going concern, $502.5M liquid resources, no LT debt, +105% OCF growth) but operationally contracting (-13% customers, -5% large customers, third consecutive accelerating RIF at 4%->3%->12%, -400bps subscription gross margin) with two notable honesty-alpha catches: (1) Mode-B SEVERE — Founder/Chairman Ragy Thomas + Director Neeraj Agrawal + other execs executed $97.4M of insider DISTRIBUTION in trailing 12mo, mostly discretionary (non-10b5-1) at $7.13-$7.78 trough prices while the company simultaneously bought back stock at $8.54 avg, creating a documented price-information asymmetry against shareholders; (2) Mode-A MODERATE — active securities class action (Boshart, S.D.N.Y.) specifically alleging undisclosed risks in Sprinklr Service product suite remains unresolved 21+ months post-filing, motion to dismiss fully briefed and pending. The $200M new buyback authorization with 62% deployed in 48 hours via ASR signals defensive (not opportunistic) capital allocation. Megacap namecheck returned ZERO hits across 17 large enterprise customers despite '59% of the Fortune 100' claim — consistent with small per-customer footprint but undermines enterprise-platform narrative weight. Composite 0.875 (2 PASS, 5 MOD, 1 SEV) — quality SaaS that has stopped growing and is being quietly distributed by insiders into a buyback-supported price.
